focusDirective: the ghost-triggered release standing alone with a tighter learned bound; placement observable on the release's own landing
admittedFrom: tmp/loop/lite/judged-80.json (blind judge, rank 1 net 7 with the rank 2 nested cell built in the same session)

hypothesis.title: A restart arms a trigger; the first acted dead-incarnation entry from the restarted node at a live peer releases every other node's still-held planned crash one step later, bounded by the learned ghost-lag p75, with no uniform pull
hypothesis.description: Standalone form of the closed nested cell, without the parent pull. Bit ghostReleasedCrash = 1 << 4 (the retired staleOrder row renamed in VARIANT_BITS; the closed pull's rename was never merged) on a salted half of fault_timing::is_placed runs, run-cap probes exempt by inheritance, cell membership following the run's placed crash arm as the retained restart_pull::cell_of does. Reused from research/lite/patches/restart-pull: restart_pull.rs whole (renamed ghost_release.rs) minus pulled_target and pull_holds - the per-scope ghost-lag learner (256 one-step cells, 200-sample floor, doubling checkpoints, decay, reset, fed by stock run-cap probes only, the sample being entry_step minus the origin's SendLedger.last_restart_step at message entries from a dead incarnation of a live origin at a live destination other than the origin), the Trigger and RunState structs, the salted coin, the delivery-site hook note_restart_pull_entry placed right after `acted` is computed in core/scheduler.rs, expire_trigger at the top of crash_hold_mask, note_restart_pull_apply at the crash apply site, the last_restart_step ledger field, the run_variant join and the util_stats export shape. Changes: (a) the learner's QUANTILE becomes a per-read argument and the run reads Q = the p75 (ScopeAccum::estimate(0.75)); both the p50 and p75 gauges are published so the median is measured; (b) at every restart apply of p at step s in recover_crashed_node, if any other node n has crash_pending > 0 and crash_hold_until[n] > s, a trigger {origin: p, restart_step: s, expires: s + Q} is armed (superseding one still armed, counted) - no hold is moved at arming; (c) at the delivery-site hook, the first message entry after s at a live node v != p from p's dead incarnation (r.origin_incarnation != incarnation(p)) whose state token changed (`acted`) sets crash_hold_until[n] = min(crash_hold_until[n], step + 1) for every n != p with crash_pending > 0, records ghost_node = v and disarms the trigger; a firing that shortens no hold is counted separately (fired_nothing_held); (d) at s + Q the trigger expires and every crash keeps its original target - nothing is ever moved later. The phase stage (crash_phase Early/Mid/Stock on the anchored half) and the ghost-absorber retarget at apply are untouched: the released crash's Pending slot draws at the first hold() past step + 1, and the retarget's ranking already prefers v (the most recent acted ghost mark). No random draw is added, so treated and untreated twins keep every stream in step. Counters under crash_place.ghost_release: armed, fired, fired_nothing_held, expired, superseded, steps_from_restart_sum, released_crashes, restarts_with_held_crash, lag_samples, gauges lag_p50, lag_p75, scopes_engaged; per cell (untreated, treated, and the nested cells of the two sibling hypotheses) runs, steps_used_sum, crashes_applied, later_crashes_applied, applied_within_3_of_acted_ghost (a crash applied at most 3 steps after the run's most recent acted fault-crossing message entry anywhere, tracked in a new State field last_acted_ghost_step set where `ghost` and `acted` are both true), fired_crashes_applied, fired_crashes_on_ghost_node. No config field.
hypothesis.rationale: The iteration 79 read on 258,000 treated placed runs was depth9 1.2056 [1.0372, 1.4014] and inside it the trigger half read depth9 1.179 and depth10 1.195 over the pull-only half (593 against 501, 78 against 65), while the pull itself barely moved placement (applied_within_window 0.687 against 0.563 on a 161-step window). Three facts from the retained patch say the trigger is the working part and was starved by the pull: (1) note_restart_pull_entry only shortened holds of crashes in pulled_mask, and pull_holds put a crash there only when its target lay past s + 161, so the trigger never touched a crash whose target already fell inside the window - the standalone release shortens every held crash, and arming at every restart with a held crash raises the occasion count from 39,751 armed to about 208,000 (restarts_with_held_crash 208,488 on 325,699 pulling-cell runs, 0.64 per run); (2) trigger.steps_from_restart_sum / fired = 222,707 / 18,471 = 12.1 steps, so firings cluster at the near end of a distribution whose p90 is 161 - a p75 bound loses few firings and stops the 21,280 expired triggers from holding a crash to the window's end; (3) the retained trigger cell's fired/armed was 0.465 against a 0.35 clause. Without the pull there is no too-early landing: the pull read depth5 0.989 and depth6 0.988 because it moved crashes ahead of the ghost; a release fired by the acted entry cannot land a crash before that entry. The oracle path is exactly the trigger's event class: label 4 is the first-crashed node's stranded record delivered at a peer, label 5 that peer's crash with its reaction in flight; the cache converts 4 to 5 at 0.205 (174,086 -> 35,694) after 3 to 4 at 0.99. 92 percent of sends in flight at a crash are still in flight at the restart (recoveries_with_own_prior_sends_inflight 1,194,550 against crashes_with_own_sends_inflight 1,289,999), so the restart anchor covers the ordering the DAG leaves open between the first delivery and the restart. Baseline per-run rates: depth8 14,281 / 790,380, depth9 2,282, depth10 421 on seed 1000; 12,341 / 1,935 / 254 on seed 1001.
hypothesis.generalityArgument: The event class is generic: a node came back from a crash, and a record its dead incarnation sent changed the state of a live peer - the peer is now reacting to stale traffic, and a crash landing on the reactor at that moment strands a stale reply, which is the shape of every recovery-timing race. It names no handler, role or timer label, is bounded by a quantity learned from the workload, moves crashes only earlier, draws nothing, and does nothing on protocols where dead-incarnation entries never act (the trigger expires and the crash keeps its target).

hypothesis.notes: Supersedes the closed pair restart-pulls-held-crash-into-learned-ghost-lag-window and pulled-crash-released-at-first-acted-ghost-entry as the restart-window mechanism: it keeps their trigger, learner and hooks and drops the uniform pull that read flat on placement. Bit 1 << 4 is free on the merged tree (the closed pull's rename lived only in its unmerged super.patch). The two sibling hypotheses in this file are nested cells inside this bit's treated half, each on its own salt, crossing each other; the implementer builds all three in one session or this one alone. Not a co-occurrence gate: the placement observable is a per-crash distance to the most recent acted ghost entry, counted on both cells.
hypothesis.redTeam: The lead's depth9 read (1.21 [1.04, 1.40] treated over untreated; trigger over pull-only 1.18 on 593 against 501 events, z about 2.7 before the 1.3 over-dispersion) was produced by crashes that had been PULLED from far targets (mean 137 steps saved) to s+161 and then released on the ghost entry; the standalone extends the release to crashes whose targets already sat inside the window, a population the lead never measured (60 percent of restarts with a held crash were not pulled), and drops the pull that the retained data cannot separate from the trigger on the primary rung (depth8 1.048 [0.987, 1.113], unresolved). Second, arming only at a restart means a ghost that reaches v BEFORE p restarts (the DAG leaves the order of recover_nl and deliver_svc_1_to_2 open) arms nothing at the right moment, and the next acted dead-incarnation entry from p after the restart may be at the other peer, so the release lands the crash on the wrong node in that share; the retarget only fixes it on the ghostAbsorberRetarget half. Third, on three nodes the release shortens EVERY other held crash, so on the runs that hold two (about 7 percent of firings by the retained pull arithmetic) both peers of the restarted node go down together, which the reply-wait analysis says leaves nobody to answer; the single-onto-absorber cell is the only guard. Fourth, the p75 bound is unmeasured (the learner exports only lag_p90 on the retained patch); with the firing mean at 12 steps a tighter bound loses few firings, but the sample is right-skewed and a p75 near 60-100 steps still holds a crash that would otherwise apply earlier - no, it does not: at expiry the crash keeps its ORIGINAL target and a crash whose target arrives first simply applies, so the expiring path is identity, which dilutes rather than harms. Fifth, the primary rung has read unresolved on 258,000 treated runs; the standalone doubles the occasions but the mechanism's effect on the objective rung may still sit inside [0.98, 1.10] and the session would rest on the advance rung alone, as the stall-release merge did.
hypothesis.scoreReason: An elaboration of the recorded lead that keeps the mechanism that produced the measured reads (the trigger, the learner, the delivery-site hook, the expiry in crash_hold_mask, the apply census; verified line by line against research/lite/patches/restart-pull) and drops the uniform pull that read flat on placement (within-window 1.22x against 2.0x) and slightly down on depth 5/6 (0.989/0.988). Every checkable figure verified: restarts_with_held_crash 208,488 on 325,699; trigger armed 39,751 / fired 18,471 / expired 21,280; steps_from_restart_sum 222,707 (12.1 per firing); retarget-stratum landing 14,681 of 18,293 and stock 728 of 1,476; recoveries_with_own_prior_sends_inflight 1,194,550 against crashes_with_own_sends_inflight 1,289,999; sender_restarted acted 810,690 on 790,380 runs; depth counts 14,281 / 2,282 / 421 and the 4->5 (0.205) and 8->9 (0.16) conversions on the cache; bit 1<<4 retired and unread. The claim that the retained code only shortened pulled_mask holds is true (note_restart_pull_entry loops over pulled_mask, pull_holds adds only targets past s + window). The event class matches the oracle's label 4 -> 5 edge without naming a handler. Composition only, no draw, clean internal contrast. Marked down from the top for the unmeasured extension to unpulled crashes and the p75 bound, and because the primary-rung read is likely to resolve neither way again at this share, leaving the advance rung to carry it. Rewritten: fired counts only firings that shortened a hold; the placement observable is the release's own landing (within 3 steps of the most recent acted ghost, per later crash, both cells, 2.5x expected, 2.0x refutes) plus the fired-crash within-3 share by crashPhase stratum; a fired-crash in-flight census is added so the at-send sibling's premise is measured before it is built; the cost clause reads against the cache median. Stands first in the family; the single-onto-absorber cell is built with it; the at-send cell waits.

nestedHypothesis.title: The ghost-triggered release moves exactly one held crash, the one that lands on the peer that took the acted ghost, and leaves every other held crash at its target
nestedHypothesis.description: Nested cell inside held-crash-released-at-first-acted-ghost-entry-after-restart's treated half by its own salt (half of it, about 0.23 of runs), bit ghostReleaseSingleOntoAbsorber = 1 << 28 (the retired clientProgressRelease row renamed; set only together with 1 << 4). At firing on v, instead of shortening every held crash: (1) if v itself has a held planned crash (send_ledger[v].crash_pending > 0), that crash alone is released to step + 1; (2) otherwise, if the run retargets (state.retarget.enabled) and the absorber ranking read on the current ledgers (absorber_decision, the same function the hold-time read and the apply use) would move some held crash n onto v (Choice::Retarget { node: v }), the first such n by index is released alone; (3) otherwise, if v is live, has no pending pair (retarget.has_pending_pair(v) false) and no held crash of its own, the first held crash n by index is released to step + 1 and RunState.forced_victim = Some((n, v)) is set; at the crash apply site, before retarget_crash, a planned crash n with forced_victim == Some((n, v)) and v still live with no pending pair is applied to v (counted under victim_swap as Applied { acted: true } through a new record_victim_swap outcome ForcedOntoAbsorber), else the stock path runs; (4) if none of the three cases holds, nothing is released and the trigger stays armed until s + Q. Every other held crash keeps its original target. Reused: everything the parent hypothesis reuses, plus retarget_crash and absorber_decision in core/scheduler.rs and ghost_absorber::choose unchanged. Counters under crash_place.ghost_release.single: released_own_crash, released_via_ranking, released_forced, no_release_case, and per-cell runs, steps_used_sum, crashes_applied, fired_crashes_applied, fired_crashes_on_ghost_node, double_crash_after_release (a second crash applied within 8 steps of a released one while the released victim is still down). No config field.
nestedHypothesis.rationale: The retained trigger released every pulled crash at once and let the apply-time retarget decide the landing: on the retarget stratum 14,681 of 18,293 fired crashes landed on v (0.80), on the stock stratum 728 of 1,476 (0.49), and the two strata split 18,293 to 1,476, so the retarget is on for about 92 percent of fired crashes. The leak is therefore small but of two kinds this cell closes: (a) the ranking passes v over when it has a pending pair or its own queued crash (victim_swap.skipped_pending_pair 38,845 per chunk, victim_crashed_holds 534,927), and in the retained code v's own queued crash was released alongside n's, so with three planned crashes on three nodes both other nodes could go down together right after p's restart - on three nodes that leaves nobody to answer the restarted node (label 7 needs the Recovery delivered to a live peer), which is the double-crash the queued reply-wait entry also targets; pulls per pulling restart were about 1.07 (85,326 pulls over about 80,000 pulling restarts), so about 7 percent of firings held two crashes; (b) on the stock stratum the crash lands on the plan victim, which is v only half the time on three nodes. Releasing one crash and landing it on v converts the release into the oracle's label 5 (the absorber's crash) deterministically and leaves the run's other crashes for later phases, where the DAG has no further crash before label 13. The pooled read is diluted by the 92 percent already landing on v, so the bands are narrow and the sharper reads are the double-crash count and the stock-stratum landing share.
nestedHypothesis.generalityArgument: The rule is stated on generic classes only: the node that reacted to a stale record is the one crashed, one crash per reaction, the others untouched. It reuses the existing absorber ranking and its liveness and pending-pair guards, adds no draw, moves no hold later, and on protocols where the ranking already picks the reactor it reduces to the parent.

At a firing on v: (1) if v has a held planned crash of its own (send_ledger[v].crash_pending > 0 and crash_hold_until[v] > step), that crash alone is released to step + 1; (2) else if the run retargets and absorber_decision on the current ledgers would move some held crash n onto v (Choice::Retarget { node: v }), the first such n by index is released alone; (3) else if v is live with no pending pair and no held crash of its own, the first held crash n by index is released to step + 1 and RunState.forced_victim = Some((n, v)); at the crash apply site, before retarget_crash, a planned crash n with forced_victim == Some((n, v)) and v still live with no pending pair is applied to v and counted under a new victim_swap outcome ForcedOntoAbsorber (Applied { acted: true }), else the stock path runs; (4) otherwise nothing is released and the trigger stays armed until s + Q. Every other held crash keeps its original target. Counters under crash_place.ghost_release.single: releases (= released_own_crash + released_via_ranking + released_forced), no_release_case, and per cell runs, steps_used_sum, crashes_applied, fired_crashes_applied, fired_crashes_on_ghost_node, double_crash_after_release (a second crash applied within 8 steps of a released one while the released victim is still down). Read against the release-all half, probe-free, matched on crashPhase, ghostAbsorberRetarget and the sibling bit: depth>=8 per run in [1.00, 1.15] pooled; depth>=9 in [1.00, 1.30]; depth>=10 in [0.95, 1.50]; on the ghostAbsorberRetarget = 0 stratum depth>=8 in [1.05, 1.35], reported with its interval. nestedHypothesis.notes: Case (3) is the only part that changes a victim on runs that do not retarget; it reaches at most the stock stratum (about 8 percent of fired crashes), so the firing floor for released_forced is grounded on 1,476 stock-stratum fired crashes in the retained chunk at a 0.22 share, scaled to this cell's occasions (about 0.25 released per run on 160,000 runs, times the stock share), not on the parent's floor. If the judge prefers a cell without any victim change, drop case (3) and keep (1)-(2); the double-crash read survives.
nestedHypothesis.redTeam: Ninety-two percent of fired crashes already ran on the retarget stratum and 80 percent of those landed on v, so the cell differs from its parent on a thin slice: the 7 percent of firings that held two crashes and the stock stratum's half that landed on the plan victim. A depth contrast diluted that far cannot separate in one session; the depth>=8 band [1.00, 1.15] will read unresolved and the cell's value is the double-crash count and the stock-stratum landing share, which are censuses, not rung evidence. Case (3) changes the plan victim on runs that do not retarget, a new behaviour the ghost-absorber retarget was merged to test on its own bit; a forced landing on a stock run confounds the ghostAbsorberRetarget = 0 stratum read the candidate itself names as the sharp one.
